newsitem.title: CANADA: CUBA EXPECTED TO PARTICIPATE FULLY IN 1999 PAN AM GAMES.
newsitem.headline: CUBA EXPECTED TO PARTICIPATE FULLY IN 1999 PAN AM GAMES.

text.p: Pan American Games organisers and Cuban sport officials say they expect full participation by the island nation in the 1999 Games in Canada despite current tensions between Cuba and the United States.
Early last week, Cuba at the last minute pulled out of an annual series of U.S.-Cuba baseball games in the United States after two bombs exploded at Havana hotels.

However, when asked whether such tensions would affect Cuba's role in the 1999 Pan Am Games in Winnipeg, Pan-American Sports Organisation (PASO) president Mario Vazquez Rana of Mexico said: "I don't think so, definitely not."
Speaking at PASO's general assembly currently underway in Winnipeg, the Manitoba provincial capital at the geographic centre of Canada, he added: "Cuba will take part fully in the '99 Games, yes."
Cuban PASO executive member Jose Fernandez Alvarez said his country will send every athlete allowed. "There will be about 500 athletes alone and we'll send the best, always the best," Alvarez says.
"The preparations in Winnipeg for the 1999 Games are going well and any possible organisational problems will be resolved," he said.
At these annual meetings, PASO received a report on the plans for the 1999 Pan Am Games and Vazquez Rana expressed confidence they would be well run.

"It is usually two years out that problems arise with planning and budgets," he said, referring to reports that organisers are seeking as much as C$40 million ($30 million U.S.) on top of the C$60 million ($45 million U.S.) in government funding already committed towards the C$145 million ($107 million U.S.) project.
The original budget was pegged at C$122 million ($90 million U.S.).
"Governments always want to hold back their funding as long as possible," the PASO president said.
Vazquez Rana also announced that U.S. Olympic Committee president William Hybl had been appointed the Americas' representative for the Association of National Olympic Committees.

It was also announced that PASO would try to have the International Olympic Committee designate the Pan Am Games as the qualifier for all Pan American nations for the Summer Olympics to ensure the top athletes from all countries compete at the Pan Am Games.

The United States Olympic Committee and Canadian Olympic Committee have already committed to send their top athletes to the 1999 games and as many as 12 international federations will use the Pan Am Games in Winnipeg as qualifiers for the 2000 Summer Olympics in Sydney.

With 5,000 athletes from 42 countries of North, South and Central America and the Caribbean participating in 41 sports, the 1999 Pan Am Games will be the third largest competition ever held in North America, eclipsed only by the Summer Olympics in Los Angeles and Atlanta.
